text:
Maya R.: Hey team — we need a concise spec for the next quant-profile package format that Redwood Optimize will produce. Current qpkg variants are messy and runtime compatibility is a pain. Thoughts?

Leo: +1. We need clearly versioned profiles and a compatibility matrix for runtime, model arch, and quant backend (GPTQ/AWQ/INT8/FP8). :eyes: 

Raghu: Suggestion: separate two concerns — profile schema (metadata + metrics) and binary payload (quant weights). Schema should be semantically versioned: profile_schema: v2, qpkg: v3. That lets us change the packing w/o breaking old readers.

Olivia: Agree. We should include fields that Optimize uses for recommendations: target_cost_per_token, latency_p95_ms, accuracy_delta_on_eval (per-evalset), fallback_model_id. Also include quant_backend: [gptq, awq, int8, fp8] and quant_params hash.

Carl: We ran into runtime errors when qpkg didn't declare kv-cache layout. Must include runtime_hints: {kv_format, seq_len_alignment, prefer_fp16_kv}. Example manifest snippet:
```
qpkg_manifest_version: "3.0"
model_id: "llama-2-13B-chat"
profile_name: "latency-compact@v1"
quant_backend: "awq"
quant_params_hash: "sha256:abcd..."
target: {cost_per_token: 0.0009, p95_ms: 85}
ev_metrics: [{name: "squad_v1", delta: 0.6}, {name: "piqa", delta: 0.4}]
compat: {runtime_min: "1.7.0", runtime_max: "<2.0.0", hw: ["A100","H100","t4"]}
checksums: {manifest: "sha256:...", payload: "sha256:..."}
```

bakeoff-bot: Bakeoff summary: AWQ/INT8 mixes show similar latency but AWQ preserves more accuracy on long contexts. Full table uploaded: https://redwood.internal/bakeoffs/17798

Maya R.: Nice. For profile naming I propose: <profile_type>-<goal>@v<semver> e.g. accuracy-preserve@v1, latency-compact@v2. Keep human-friendly and machine-parseable. Avoid model names inside profile_name.

Jen P.: From product POV, Optimize should surface both recommended profiles and an explanation: why suggested (cost vs. accuracy), expected delta, and rollback instructions. The manifest should contain a short human_reason string.

Leo: On compatibility: runtime should check manifest.compat at load. If runtime version < runtime_min => reject. If runtime within range but hw missing => allow with warning and record telemetry. For fallback we should include fallback_profiles: ["accuracy-preserve@v1"] so router can automatically switch.

Olivia: Also include a small test prompt set hash and expected token-level diffs to catch silent regressions. e.g. smoke_eval_hash: "sha256:..." and smoke_eval_pass_threshold: 0.95. If runtime detected > threshold fail, flag for manual review.

Raghu: On packaging: put manifest.json (YAML allowed) + compressed payload .bin + sig.pubkey.qpkg. Signing required for private deployments. Add package layout version in manifest.

infra-bot: FYI — storage quota for qpkgs currently 75GB/month for eng-ml. Large AWQ payloads (13B+) may need staged upload. :warning: 

Carl: Implementation note — add a tiny compatibility shim in runtime to map old qpkg fields (old: model_backends => new: compat.hw) for 6 months. We'll document migration path.

Maya R.: OK action list: 1) draft profile_schema v2 (Raghu + Olivia) 2) draft qpkg manifest v3 example + naming rules (Carl + Leo) 3) Optimize UX mapping for recommendations (Jen + Maya) 4) runtime compat shims + checks (Carl + infra). I'll create a PR with the spec and a sample qpkg. Target: EOW.

Leo: I'll add unit tests for manifest parser and compat guard.

Raghu: I'll prepare conversion tool from old qpkg -> v3 for the bakeoff artifacts.

Olivia: Will add smoke_eval hash generation in the bakeoff harness.

Maya R.: Thanks all. If anyone has objections to the naming or schema fields, drop them here. Otherwise I'll open the PR in ~1h. :rocket:
